title: FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) - Band 8 (900 MHz) for UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) filter targeting Band 8 (900 MHz) for UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter. The filter is designed on 42° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 1680.6 MHz and bandwidth of 260.5 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator)
- Frequency Band: Band 8 (900 MHz)
- Application: UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter
- Substrate: 42° YX LiTaO3
- Package: SiP (System in Package)
- Design Tool: Synopsys CustomSim
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) design targeting Band 8 (900 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1680.6 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       260.5 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.4 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 15.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 41.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 25.0 dB
Q Factor:               10900
Temperature Coefficient:-27.1 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.2 x 1.0 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   4
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Synopsys CustomSim and load the FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 42° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1680.6 MHz, BW 260.5 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.4 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (SiP (System in Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, 42° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N9041B UXA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 5042 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.4 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 15.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 391 MHz offset >= 41.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 2 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 5.7 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +31 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 91%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-02-02
Devices Tested:         78
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.15 dB
Return Loss (meas):     17.4 dB
Rejection (meas):       44.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       29.6 dB
Q Factor (meas):        10900
Group Delay Variation:  4.9 ns
Power Handling:         +26 dBm
Die Yield:              92.1%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 8 (900 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Group delay flatness improved compared to previous revision.
e) Wafer-level uniformity was excellent (sigma < 1.5%).
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
